The '''TIE series''', also known as the '''TIE line''' or '''TIE fighter series''', was a series of [[starship]]s (primarily [[starfighter]]s) manufactured by [[Sienar Fleet Systems]] and later [[Sienar-Jaemus Fleet Systems]], which was distinguished by their [[twin ion engine]]s and [[solar collector]] panels.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> There existed dozens of different models notably utilized by the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="CYD2">''[[Choose Your Destiny: A Luke & Leia Adventure]]''</ref>

==History==
===Background===
The TIE line's earliest development began during the late [[Republic Era]], with [[Sienar Advanced Projects Laboratory]]'s advancements on the field of [[Ion engine|ion propulsion]]. Part of the Laboratory's classified project roster was the ''[[Scimitar]]'', a heavily modified custom [[Star Courier]] which utilized experimental high-temperature ion [[engine]]s to travel in high speeds. To solve the engines' energy consumption problem, Raith Sienar devised a system of twin folding radiator panels that were equipped in the ship's wings and provided the massive power needed while preserving its aerodynamic shape.<ref name="Manual">''[[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]]''</ref>

By the end of the [[Clone Wars]], [[Republic Sienar Systems]], Advanced Projects' parent company found itself bankrupt and ownership was transferred to the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan]]; with the Clan's dissolution after the [[Invasion of Scipio]], its holdings, including RSS were transferred to the [[Office of the Chancellor]].<ref name="Helmet Collection 49">{{HelmetCollectionCite|49|Databank A-Z}}</ref> Following the end of the war and the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], having become aware of Sienar's talent from the APL's designs uncovered during the war, decided to award Sienar the contract for the design and manufacture of the first Imperial-made [[starfighter]] to fill the ranks of the newfound [[Imperial Navy]].<ref name="Manual" /> Until then, the [[Imperial Starfighter Corps]] was composed of a variety of Republic- and privately-manufactured vessels such as [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter|Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class V-wing starfighter]]s,<ref name="Mercy Mission">{{StoryCite|story=Mercy Mission (short story)|book=The Rise of the Empire}}</ref> [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter|ARC-170]]<ref name="Tarkin" /> and [[ARC-40b Scout-Reconnaissance Fighter]]s,<ref name="SaS">''[[Savage Spirits]]''</ref> [[Alpha-class Xg-1 Star Wing|''Alpha''-class Xg-1 Star Wing]]s and [[M3-A Scyk interceptor]]s.<ref name="Starships and Speeders" />

===Development===
{{Quote|If the opposition is not intimidated by the sight of our capital ships in planetary orbit, and if a barrage from Imperial cannons does not result in the opposition's immediate surrender, the Emperor envisions that we shall unleash swarms of starfighters that will seek out and destroy any survivors.|Wilhuff Tarkin, ''Memorandum to Raith Sienar, Chief Executive Officer, SFS''|<ref name="Manual">''[[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]]''</ref>}}
[[File:TarkinTBB.png|thumb|left|300px|Moff Wilhuff Tarkin, whose memorandum to Raith Sienar marked the beginning of the TIE line]]
[[Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], the man who would later be appointed by the Emperor to serve as [[governor]] of all of the [[Outer Rim Territories]] under the title of [[Grand Moff]],<ref name="Tarkin">[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']]</ref> personally assigned the design of the project that would become the TIE line to Raith Sienar in a memorandum outlining [[Tarkin Doctrine|his doctrine]]'s main points of strength through fear.<ref name="Manual" /> Tarkin's ideology would later be dubbed the "Tarkin Doctrine" by the media.<ref name="Tarkin" /> Tarkin also laid out the basic requirements of the project: it had to be an economical, easy to manufacture and mass produce starfighter that would simultaneously strike fear in its enemies and make its [[pilot]]s dedicated and compliant to the Navy command. The starfighter, according to Tarkin, should also produce a distinctive sound designed to set it apart from other generic designs and serve as its signature in battle.<ref name="Manual" />

Upon delivery of the memorandum, the [[Admiralty (Imperial)|Imperial Admiralty]] formally itemized their requirements and budget for the new starfighter, based on Tarkin's outline, to allow Sienar to begin work on a protoype. Additional features requested were limited range and ground control systems, lack of a landing gear and [[hyperdrive]], and limited [[life support]], all measures designed to limit pilots' independence from the fleet and reduce the chances of defection. Tarkin further insisted on the craft lacking even rudimentary [[deflector shield]]ing, a standard feature in every spaceborne vessel used to protect the pilot from [[asteroid|space debris]] and [[stellar radiation]]. Despite protests from other naval officers, Palpatine himself endorsed the proposition, arguing that pilots would be encouraged to complete their missions quickly to return to the safety of their hangars.<ref name="Manual" />

[[File:TIE_Fighter_Prototype.png|thumb|240x240px|Sienar Fleet Systems' original proposal for an exclusively spaceborne TIE fighter]]
Sienar eventually started his work on the design, drawing from a number of his and [[Kuat Drive Yards]] (RSS' main opposition) designs, including his prototype Star Courier and the ''Nimbus''- and ''Actis''-class already used by the Navy. Those included the Star Courier's [[solar collector]] wings and the ''Actis''-class' spherical pressurized cockpit and twin ion engines, the latter of which were extensively tested and experimented on by Sienar until he developed a working high-performance prototype that capitalized and improved upon previous models, the [[P-s3 ion engine|P-s3]]. Sienar included those features into the plans for the first [[TIE fighter prototype]], which, according to Imperial mandates was designed to be exclusively spaceborne. In presenting the plans to the Navy, however, Sienar surprised them with an additional design for a slightly more expensive vessel which was going to also be able to function in a [[planet]]ary [[atmosphere]] as well as land on its wings. Naval command authorized Sienar to move ahead with the assembly of prototypes for both designs, the latter of which was slightly bulkier and featured stronger pylons and reinforced spars connecting the wings to the cockpit. This design was ultimately proven to be more effective that the original, and<ref name="Manual" /> in [[18 BBY]]<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> the newly formed [[Sienar Fleet Systems]] was greenlighted to begin mass assembly of the first exclusively Imperial starfighter, the Twin Ion Engine Line edition starfighter, or simply [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE/ln]].<ref name="Manual" />

===Introduction to the Navy and bent-wing advancements===
====Spread of the TIE====
[[File:TIE-Fighter-RO-SWCT.png|thumb|left|278x278px|The TIE/ln fighter, the Imperial Navy's first dedicated starfighter model]]
The TIE/ln was introduced to the Navy's starfighter forces within the same year<ref name="Timelines" /> and saw action in the [[Invasion of Mon Cala]],<ref name="Dark Lord 14">[[Darth Vader (2017) 14|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 14]]</ref> one of the earliest open conflicts fought by the Galactic Empire in the name of asserting its power. At the time of the invasion, the fighters were new. Forces such as the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Sovereign]]''{{'s}} group—which participated in the invasion—adopted some of the new SFS-produced models<ref name="Dark Lord 13">[[Darth Vader (2017) 13|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 13]]</ref> and deployed them into Mon Cala's atmosphere.<ref name="Dark Lord 14" />

As part of the five-year plan for the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim's]] industrialization, factory worlds including [[Lothal]] were charged with producing even more<ref name="Empire Day">{{Rebels|Empire Day (episode)}}</ref> to eventually replace all Republic-era starfighters in the Navy.<ref name="Manual" /> This goal was more or less completed within the same decade; by [[5 BBY]]<ref name="Date">{{AndorDate|106}}</ref> the complement of bases such as the [[Alkenzi Air Base]]<ref name="TheEye">{{Andor|The Eye}}</ref> and the [[Lothal Imperial airfield]] were entirely comprised of TIE/ln.<ref name="Flight of the Defender">{{Rebels|Flight of the Defender}}</ref> [[Grakkus's criminal empire]] designed a [[TIE Bolt|TIE-inspired podracer]] as a gift for [[Admiral]] [[Rellen]]<ref name="Beyond Victory">[[Star Wars: Beyond Victory - A Mixed Reality Playset|''Star Wars: Beyond Victory'' - A Mixed Reality Playset]]</ref> around [[10 BBY]],<ref name="10BBYDate">{{BeyondVictoryDate}}</ref> only for it to be stolen by [[Sebulba]] and destroyed.<ref name="Beyond Victory" />

====TIE/ad v1====
[[File:The_Inquisitors_TIE_Fighter.png|thumb|290x290px|The Advanced v1 was the first test of the bent-wing design, incorporating the ''Scimitar''<nowiki/>'s features]]
Despite Sienar's design being more than capable of eliminating pirate and mercenary threats when used in conjunction with Imperial [[capital ship]]s and meeting more or less all of the Navy's requirements, Raith Sienar continued experimenting with the craft and his own Star Courier design to create an even more advanced starfighter.<ref name="Manual" /> By using the folding bent-shape wings of the ''Scimitar'' and combining them with the TIE/ln's [[solar ionization reactor]] and twin ion engines, Sienar created a working prototype dubbed the [[TIE/ad v1]]. This ship was delivered to the Empire,<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> and at least four were produced and assigned to the [[Inquisitorius]] for their [[Jedi]] hunting.<ref name="TFOTF">{{Rebels|The Future of the Force}}</ref> The Navy kept the prototype in its possession and tasked ace [[Baron of the Empire|flying baron]] [[Valen Rudor]] with performing early testing of the model for a possible introduction to the fleet, but the ship was destroyed by the [[Phoenix Cell]] in a [[bombing at the Empire Day parade]] on Lothal.<ref name="Empire Day" /> Limited testing of the model continued from the [[Inquisitor]]s<ref name="SOD">{{Rebels|Shroud of Darkness}}</ref> yielding encouraging results in both atmospheric and orbital combat performance,<ref name="Manual" /> and at least one TIE/ad v1 was used by [[captain]] [[Lindon Javes]] of [[Helix Squadron]].<ref name="Squadrons">''[[Star Wars: Squadrons]]''</ref> However, a number of shortcomings (namely, the limited power supply capabilities of the wings which forced the craft to use [[fuel]] instead of the reactor)<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> as well as the loss of many prototypes to the rebels resulted in the model never being approved for mass production.<ref name="Manual" />

====TIE Advanced x1====
[[File:Vader_TIEAdvanced_SWB.png|thumb|left|280x280px|The TIE Advanced x1's design was the first to introduce the standard bent-wing design]]
Nevertheless, the v1 was considered by many in the Navy to be a groundbreaking<ref name="Baron of the Empire">{{FFGXW2|set=Galactic Empire Conversion Kit|cardname=Baron of the Empire}}</ref> and thoroughly impressive design.<ref name="Empire Day" /> At some point before [[4 BBY]],<ref name="Siege">''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Siege of Lothal]]''</ref> [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], the Emperor's enforcer and effective [[Commander-in-Chief]] of the [[Imperial High Command]] approached Sienar with schematics for an advanced starfighter based on the v1 to serve as his personnal vessel. Sienar started work on the vessel, which,<ref name="BMF 25">{{BuildFalconCite|17|Starship Fact File}}</ref> in continuing the v1's legacy<ref name="The Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref> was dubbed the [[TIE Advanced x1]].<ref name="BMF 25" /> By 4 BBY,<ref name="Siege" /> the starfighter was complete and delivered to the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]]. Following his exact specifications, the x1 was equipped with longer bent wings than the v1 which were more than capable of meeting the increased energy requirements of the TIE's added [[deflector shield]]s and [[hyperdrive]]. These were also shorter in height than the v1's, making it a smaller, more streamlined target and able to perform extreme maneuvers including sustained recoverable rolling and flying backwards. The craft was heavier in weight and firepower than both the /ln and the v1, featuring an enlarged [[durasteel]] superstructure behind the cockpit to house the hyperdrive and shield projector, and a [[cluster missile]] launcher with 20 projectiles.<ref name="BMF 25" />

Darth Vader utilized the x1 in a number of occasions with extremely positive results,<ref name="BMF 25" /> including taking out the Phoenix Cell's [[flagship]] ''[[Phoenix Home]]''<ref name="Siege" /> and nearly single-handedly determining the outcome of the [[Battle of Yavin]]. Heavily damaged during the latter, the ship was nonetheless recovered and repaired, leading to a debate within the Navy on whether or not it should be formally introduced to the fleet.<ref name="BMF 25" /> TIE Advanced prototypes, still considered a new design at that time, were at the disposal of Imperial forces based on the planet [[Tatooine]] during the [[Operations on Tatooine|Empire-Rebel struggle]] for the world. In fact, the [[Tatooine rebel cell]] was able to secure some x1s for its operations against the Empire.<ref name="Commander" /> In the end, the proposal to formally introduce the x1 into the Imperial Navy was rejected on the basis of the starfighter's very high cost<ref name="BMF 25" /> of 160,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] compared to the TIE/ln's 60,000.<ref name="Manual" />

A select few squadrons were equipped with the x1 before the project was scrapped.<ref name="BMF 25" /> Despite its limited production, however, the TIE Advanced became a favorite amongst elite pilots.<ref name="TIE Fighters">{{EncyclopediaCite|TIE Fighters}}</ref> Indeed, an [[Ace]] of [[Storm Squadron]] flew the starfighter at one point.<ref name="X-wing">{{FFGXW2|set=TIE Advanced x1 Expansion Pack|cardname=Storm Squadron Ace}}</ref> Despite the formal end of the project,<ref name="BMF 25" /> Vader would also continue to fly his x1.<ref name="Vader 16">[[Darth Vader (2020) 16|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 16]]</ref> A TIE fighter with the central design of a regular TIE fighter but wings<ref name="Star Wars 8">[[Star Wars (2020) 8|''Star Wars'' (2020) 8]]</ref> akin to those of an x1<ref name="Siege" /> was part of the [[Hunter Fleet]] and fought in the [[Battle at Elessia]].<ref name="Star Wars 8" />

===Production of specialized variants===
====TIE bomber====
[[File:Wedge_TIE_bomber.jpg|thumb|290x290px|A TIE/sa flying above Skystrike Academy]]
While Sienar experimented with the TIE Advanced line, the Imperial Navy started encountering the first issues with the TIE/ln. The vessel was designed for short-range operations, but mission requirements started increasingly forcing pilots to fly further away from their [[capital ship]]s and stretching the TIE's capabilities. Furthermore, the TIE/ln was not properly equipped for ground attack operations, forcing the Navy to use [[Star Destroyer]]s, whose weapons proved to be overpowered and messy for precision bombing.<ref name="Manual" /> After unsuccessfully attempting to solve the problem with a modification to the TIE/ln<ref name="Complete Vehicles 2018">[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]]</ref> dubbed the [[TIE/gt]],<ref name="BMF 51">{{BuildFalconCite|51|Starship Fact File}},</ref> the Navy eventually decided to task Sienar with producing a dedicated bomber. Sienar Fleet Systems responded with the TIE Surface Assault Bomber, code-named the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|TIE/sa]].<ref name="Manual" />

The new model was equipped with the elongated bent-wing design previously tested with the TIE/x1, and was properly equipped for independent long-range operations<ref name="Manual" /> -although it still lacked a hyperdrive.<ref name="BMF 51" /> It was layed out in a twin-pod design, with the starboard-side carrying the pilot and [[flight computer]]s, and the port-side one carrying heavy ammunition including [[concussion missile]]s,<ref name="Manual" /> [[proton torpedo]]es,<ref name="BMF 51" /> [[thermal detonator]]s,<ref name="TIE model set">''[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter Deluxe Book and Model Set]]''</ref> [[proton bomb]]s and [[space mine]]s.<ref name="Manual" /> Sienar also equipped the TIE/sa with a [[398X bomb sight]] and a [[T-s7b targeting computer]] developed specifically for precision bombing<ref name="TIE model set" /> in orbital and atmospheric conditions. The new bomber was welcomed by the fleet<ref name="Manual" /> and by [[11 BBY]] it was actively being used in anti-capital ship operations,<ref name="AND">[[A New Dawn (novel)|''A New Dawn'']]</ref> independent and squadron-based low and high atmospheric attacks and surgical sabotage strikes.<ref name="Manual" />

====TIE Interceptor====
[[File:TIEinterceptor-FansChoice2020.png|thumb|left|290px|The TIE/IN interceptor, the Navy's most advanced mass-produced starfighter model]]
Although the Navy's TIE/ln and TIE/sa proved more than capable of handling the insurgents and pirates that plagued the Empire during the first years of its rule, the [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|emerging rebellion]] began to slowly turn the tide of orbital combat with shielded, faster and more maneuverable starfighters including the [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|BTL-A4 Y-wing starfighter]]<ref name="Manual" /> reclaimed from the Republic's reserves<ref name="Steps">''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]''</ref> and most importantly the extremely fast [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor]]. Eventually, the Naval leadership considered the introduction of an improved model of starfighter that would be able to match their rebel opponents. Again,<ref name="BMF 33">{{BuildFalconCite|33|Starship Fact File}}</ref> the engineers of<ref name="X-wing" /> Sienar Fleet Systems fulfilled the Navy's request with the [[TIE/IN interceptor]],<ref name="BMF 33" /> the next TIE design Sienar tackled after the x1.<ref name="X-wing" />

The TIE/IN was essentially a stripped-down version of the TIE/x1, lacking the hyperdrive, shielding and extended reinforced superstructure of the original prototype. It nonetheless retained<ref name="BMF 33" /> many of the x1's best qualities,<ref name="X-wing" /> including the improved engines, solar collector cells, and same bent-wing design, which was further improved by opening a horizontal hole in the middle of the wings to increase pilot visibility. The dagger-shaped craft was powered by an improved [[I-a3a solar ionization reactor]]<ref name="BMF 33" /> connected to an [[autothruster]],<ref name="Reinforcements of Renown">{{FantasyFlightGames|url=en/news/2021/2/15/reinforcements-of-renown|text=Reinforcements of Renown}}</ref> which allowed the TIE/IN to perform tight maneuvers impossible in most other craft. Its firepower was also increased<ref name="BMF 33" /> with four all-new [[L-s9.3 laser cannon]]s on the wingtips,<ref name="TIE model set" /> which allowed it to be more than a match for rebel starfighters. Continuing the tradition of Inquisitorius pilots being the first to test new vessels, the Imperial Navy assigned a [[TIE/IN Interceptor Prototype|prototype]] of the TIE/IN to the [[Second Sister]] who performed extensive trial runs<ref name="Galaxy of Heroes">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''</ref> and also used it to investigate reports of a [[Jedi]] on [[Bracca]].<ref name="Fallen Order">''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]''</ref> The trials' positive results encouraged the Imperial leadership, and the TIE/IN soon entered production as the Navy's third mass-produced starfighter after the TIE/ln and TIE/sa.<ref name="BMF 33" />

[[File:Tie_interceptors_mandalorian.png|thumb|290x290px|A TIE/IN squadron of the Imperial Remnant]]
The TIE/IN officially entered service with the Imperial Navy in [[3 BBY]],<ref name="Dev insights date">{{EA|subdomain=forums.galaxy-of-heroes.starwars|url=discussion/253434/developer-insights-tie-in-interceptor-prototype|text=Developer Insights: TIE/IN interceptor Prototype}} establishes that the TIE/IN interceptor saw its formal first deployment three [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin]], which corresponds to [[3 BBY]] according to ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''.</ref> while the x1 was still being developed as a prototype.<ref name="Commander" /> The interceptor was first fielded within elite units, such as the [[128th Fighter Group]] and the [[181st Imperial Fighter Wing]], and to TIE/ln squadron [[commander]]s for combat testing. The new fighters proved to be extremely effective.<ref name="BMF 33" /> By the time of the [[Battle of Hoth]] in [[3 ABY]], they started to slowly replace TIE/ln as the preferred starfighter-to-starfighter combat craft, with TIE/IN making up one-fifth of the Imperial starfighter fleet by [[4 ABY]].<ref name="Starfighters">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles]]''</ref>

====TIE Defender Project====
[[File:Thrawn-1-Animation_textless.png|thumb|left|250px|Grand Admiral Thrawn, father of the Defender Project]]
By around [[2 BBY]],<ref name="2 BBY Date">''[[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]]'' states that [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] began the TIE/D Defender project two [[Standard year|years]] before the completion of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|first Death Star]], which corresponds to [[2 BBY]] per ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]''. Therefore, the TIE/D Defender was first used in 2 BBY.</ref> it was apparent to the Imperial High Command that the newly-introduced [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]]<ref name="DRVG">''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> as well as [[Declaration of the Rebel Alliance|the formation]] of a coherent and organized [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] had resulted in a rapidly evolved orbital combat theater.<ref name="Manual" /> While the Emperor seemed to side with the [[Imperial Military Department of Advanced Weapons Research]]'s continued development of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 battle station]] as a solution to the rebel threat,<ref name="Thrawn: Alliances" /> [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] started investigating the [[Imperial Security Bureau]]'s interrogations of attempted defectors from the [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot]] corps to identify common grounds. What he discovered was that nearly all defectors reported a growing reluctance to pilot unshielded, badly defended and fleet-dependent craft like the standard TIE/ln.<ref name="Manual" /> 

In response, the Grand Admiral spearheaded an initiative to develop a well-defended and armed, hyperdrive-equipped shielded fighter that would be able to operate independently from the fleet and strike behind enemy lines, mimicking the Rebels' tactics to the Empire's advantage. Furthermore, in an official report submitted to Grand Moff Tarkin, Thrawn outlined that the project would not only be advantageous against rebel pilots, but also increase the loyalty of the Imperial pilots. Development of the classified project began in the [[Sienar Advanced Projects Laboratory|Sienar Systems Advanced Projects Laboratory]] on Lothal<ref name="Manual" /> in 2 BBY,<ref name="2 BBY Date" /> where Thrawn submitted very specific design aspects for the starfighter, including a tri-wing design incorporating three sets of inverted TIE/IN wings mounted further away from the cockpit to increase visibility.<ref name="Manual" /> Thrawn based his design on a prototype high-powered starfighter submitted years ago by industrialist [[Morgan Elsbeth]] and at the time rejected by [[Moff]] [[Isdain]], taking note of the design's unique layout of emphasis on starfighter warfare.<ref name="Anger">{{TOTE|The Path of anger}}</ref> Reports from several SFS engineers suggested that Thrawn even displayed a rare [[Kamino saberdart]] to demonstrate the wings' orientation and its effectiveness. Computer simulations of the proposed design confirmed the speed and maneuverability advantages of the layout, and an experimental prototype was assembled for flight tests and dubbed the [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter]].<ref name="Manual" />

[[File:TIEDefender-MF48.png|thumb|300px|right|The TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter was a initially designed by Morgan Elsbeth.]]
The prototype was combat-tested<ref name="Manual" /> by veteran [[flight instructor]] [[Vult Skerris]] of the [[Skystrike Academy]] during [[Operation Handoff]], where it was able to reach a rebel convoy carrying rebel leader [[Mon Mothma]] via its hyperdrive and then outgun the escorting [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron's]] Y-wings, destroying two of them. Although it was heavily damaged by the [[Archeon Nebula]]'s gases,<ref name="Secret Cargo">{{Rebels|Secret Cargo}}</ref> it was later also flown by Darth Vader during the [[Imperial–Grysk conflict]], with the Dark Lord admiring its effectiveness himself. Vader personally reported on the project to the Emperor, expressing his support, and suggested a number of improvements including heavier weapons and simplified controls,<ref name="Thrawn: Alliances">''[[Thrawn: Alliances]]''</ref> which the SFS engineers were quick to implement.<ref name="Manual" />

With both the Emperor and members of the High Command including Tarkin and [[Admiral]] [[Balanhai Savit]] supporting the project while simultaneously disproving of [[Project Stardust]]'s (the DS-1 development division) costly delays,<ref name="Thrawn: Treason">''[[Thrawn: Treason]]''</ref> work started anew on the Defender project, with an improved prototype based on Vader's suggestions<ref name="Jedi Night">{{Rebels|Jedi Night}}</ref> being ready by [[1 BBY]]<ref name="Approx">The trivia guide for ''[[Star Wars Rebels: Heroes of Mandalore]]'' states that [[Bo-Katan Kryze]] was redesigned to advance the character's age by "18 [[Standard year|years]] or so." As she was last seen was in ''[[The Lawless]]'', which was dated to [[19 BBY]] by ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'', it can be assumed that the events of ''Heroes of Mandalore'' take place in approximately 1 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. As "Flight of the Defender" takes place shortly after ''Heroes of Mandalore'', it can be assumed it is also around the [[Standard year|year]] 1 BBY.</ref> and codenamed the [[TIE/D Defender Elite]]. Intended to become the Imperial Navy's next-generation response to the rebel threat, the model was equipped with eight TIE/IN L-s9.3 [[heavy laser cannon]]s, a [[warhead]] launcher with six [[missile]]s, a [[tractor beam projector]], advanced [[P-sz9.7 twin ion engine]]s and a dedicated [[CRX-9 targeting computer]], all developed specifically for the prototype.<ref name="Manual" />

The design was extensively tested on [[flight simulator]]s against virtually all fighters used by the rebels at the time, and found to vastly outperform all of them. Official flight tests using the first assembled prototype were scheduled to be performed<ref name="Manual" /> during that same year,<ref name="Approx" /> with both Lothal's Governor [[Arihnda Pryce]] and Grand Admiral Thrawn attending and Vult Skerris piloting.<ref name="Manual" /> However, the local [[Lothal resistance group|resistance group]] led by former governor [[Ryder Azadi]] managed to steal the technical plans of the original TIE/D prototype and inform [[Alliance High Command]] of the project's development. After Alliance officers including [[Hera Syndulla]] analyzed the plans, they determined that mass-production of the fighter would result in their starfighter forces being quickly decimated,<ref name="An Inside Man">{{Rebels|An Inside Man}}</ref> as they had no way of defeating the advanced starfighter;<ref name="Crawlers">{{Rebels|Crawler Commandeers}}</ref> thus, destroying the project became a priority.<ref name="Manual" /> Phoenix cell operatives [[Ezra Bridger]] and [[Sabine Wren]] managed to infiltrate the site of the first official flight test and steal the TIE/D Elite prototype before Skerris had boarded it.<ref name="Flight of the Defender">{{Rebels|Flight of the Defender}}</ref>

Thrawn saw the opportunity for an impromptu live-fire test,<ref name="Manual" /> and dispatched three of the airfield's elite TIE/IN to pursue them, with the untrained Bridger being able to shoot down all three using the Elite's advanced weapons. Pryce [[kill switch|remotely disabled]] the prototype, causing it to crash, and Thrawn determined the test to be a success, as the craft was advanced enough to allow even an unskilled pilot such as Bridger<ref name="Flight of the Defender" /> to defeat elite Imperial pilots.<ref name="Manual" />

[[File:Skerris-Death-RA.jpg|thumb|left|280x280px|The destruction of Vult Skerris' TIE/D Elite prototype over Lothal]]
Despite the Defender Elite's excellent performance, another elite prototype was destroyed in a massive rebel [[attack on Lothal]] determined to destroy the project's factories and stop it from going live. Although Thrawn's blockade was successful in intercepting and destroying the invading X-wings, the TIE/D was caught in the ''[[Chimaera]]''{{'s}} friendly fire and crashed,<ref name="Rebel Assault">{{Rebels|Rebel Assault}}</ref> while a significant part of the groundside assembly lines were bombed and disabled. Amidst [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]]'s insistence that Project Stardust should take priority over the now uncovered Defender project,<ref name="Manual" /> Tarkin advised Thrawn to make a case directly to the Emperor to ensure the project's continuation. With the Grand Admiral and his forces off-world, the Phoenix cell attempted a final attack on Lothal's [[Capital City]], during which governor Pryce intentionally destroyed the [[Lothal City fuel depot]] in an attempt to capture them. This strategic mistake depleted the remaining Defender Elite factories from critical resources needed to continue development of the starfighter,<ref name="DUME">{{Rebels|DUME}}</ref> and the project was scrapped,<ref name="Manual" /> with all funding ultimately directed to development of Project Stardust.<ref name="Thrawn: Treason" /> 

Tarkin stated that the Defender would be the next in production line as soon as the [[superweapon]] was complete,<ref name="Thrawn: Treason" /> but Thrawn's disappearance in the [[Liberation of Lothal]]<ref name="Family & Farewell">{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}}</ref> and Tarkin's death in the Battle of Yavin<ref name="IV">{{Film|IV}}</ref> left the project without direction. The entire Defender line was decommissioned,<ref name="Bounty Hunters 19">[[Bounty Hunters 19|''Bounty Hunters'' 19]]</ref> yet Defenders still saw some use as the Galactic Civil War continued.<ref name="Commander" /><ref name="Bounty Hunters 19" /> Indeed, some advancements were made, such as the development of a new model dubbed the [[TIE Advanced x7]]. However, it did not advance from the prototype stage due to all six examples being destroyed in the Battle of Hoth.<ref name="BMF 48">{{BuildFalconCite|48|Starship Fact File}}</ref> Additionally, five TIE Defenders<ref name="Bounty Hunters 19" /> were used by the [[Dark Squadron]] under [[Beilert Valance]]<ref name="Bounty Hunters 18">[[Bounty Hunters 18|''Bounty Hunters'' 18]]</ref> around the same time.<ref name="4ABY date">The events of [[Bounty Hunters 19|''Bounty Hunters'' 19]] take place between [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' places in [[3 ABY]] and [[4 ABY]] respectively.</ref>

==Variants==
===Galactic Empire===
====Starfighters & bombers====
[[File:TIEBrute-MF90.png|thumb|250px|right|A TIE/rb heavy starfighter]]
As well as the TIE/ln, Imperial [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot|pilots]] would make use of [[flight simulator]]s and [[TIE training drone]]s for training purposes.<ref name="The Antilles Extraction">{{Rebels|The Antilles Extraction}}</ref><ref name="Shadow Fall">''[[Shadow Fall: An Alphabet Squadron Novel]]''</ref> One TIE variant was the [[TIE/rb heavy starfighter]], a bulked-up version of the TIE/ln with heavier armor as well as a secondary pod which housed a [[MGK-300 integrated droid brain]]<ref name="SWZ">{{FFGXW2|set=TIE/rb Heavy Expansion Pack|cardname=Target-Assist MGK-300}}</ref> and had mounted heavy laser cannons.<ref name="RB Databank">{{Databank|imperial-heavy-tie-fighter|Imperial heavy TIE fighter}}</ref>

Another early TIE variant was the [[TIE/gt]], which eventually evolved into the more prominent [[TIE/sa tactical bomber]], with inward-bent wings and a second pod to carry ordnance.<ref name="Complete Vehicles 2018">[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]]</ref> A heavy variant was the [[TIE/ca "Punisher" Starfighter]], which contained quadruple the payload of the TIE bomber.<ref name="Starships and Speeders" /> The [[TIE/fc]], [[TIE/sr]], [[TIE/rc]],<ref name="TIE Fighters">{{EncyclopediaCite|TIE Fighters}}</ref> and [[TIE scout]] were models used for reconnaissance missions.<ref name="Alphabet Squadron">[[Alphabet Squadron (novel)|''Alphabet Squadron'']]</ref> While it resembled a TIE/ln, it featured a [[hyperdrive]] to allow for long-range travel.<ref name="TROS Junior Novel">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: A Junior Novel]]''</ref>

====Shuttles & transports====
[[File:TIE_boarding_craft-TFOWM.png|thumb|left|250px|A TIE boarding craft]]
The [[TIE/sh shuttle]]<ref name="Pirate's Price">''[[Pirate's Price]]''</ref> was derived from the TIE bomber and maintained its two-pod configuration, with the second pod built to carry passengers between capital ships. It was identified by its wings, which were distinctively bent outward. Another TIE shuttle variant was the [[TIE boarding craft]], which more closely resembled the TIE bomber and was used for the transportation and boarding of up to two stormtrooper squads. Along with the TIE shuttle, it was one of the few TIE variants equipped with deflector shields.<ref name="Manual" />

The [[TIE lander]] was a triple-hulled TIE variant that could transport an entire company of troops.<ref name="CL 2016">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> A more unique model was the [[TIE/rp Reaper attack lander]], a shuttle used to transport elite troops to points on a battlefield.<ref name="Scarif Base Pilot card">{{FFGXW|set=TIE Reaper Expansion Pack|cardname=Scarif Base Pilot}}</ref> It featured two pointed, forward-facing wings.<ref name="Rogue One" />

====Advanced & experimental models====
[[File:DarkInk-Braver-than-Most.png|thumb|right|250px|Darth Vader atop his personal TIE Advanced x1.]]
The [[TIE/ad v1]] was an advanced starfighter prototype equipped with a hyperdrive, shields, and curved folding wings with extra armor. It commonly saw use by members of the [[Inquisitorius]].<ref name="Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref> The [[TIE Advanced x1]] was another advanced fighter with similar features, but was smaller and featured bent wings similar to the TIE bomber. [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced|One]] such model served as Darth Vader's personal starfighter.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> However, the TIE Advanced x1 was too expensive to mass-produce, so the [[TIE/IN interceptor]] was created as its successor.<ref name="SOTG">''[[Star Wars: Ships of the Galaxy]]''</ref> While it lacked a hyperdrive and shields, it featured extra laser cannons mounted on its pointed wingtips.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> The [[TIE Avenger prototype|TIE Avenger]] was also inspired by the TIE Advanced.<ref name="TIE Fighters" />

Grand Admiral Thrawn's fighter initiative on [[Lothal]] saw the development of the elite [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter]],<ref name="An Inside Man">{{Rebels|An Inside Man}}</ref> which was equipped with heavy cannons, shields, and a hyperdrive. Its characteristic three wings resembled those of the TIE Interceptor inverted, and the fighter proved a powerful combatant against rebel starfighters.<ref name="Secret Cargo">{{Rebels|Secret Cargo}}</ref> An even more powerful variant called the [[TIE/D Defender Elite]] was developed,<ref name="Defender">{{Rebels|Flight of the Defender}}</ref> but the entire project was halted by the destruction of the [[Lothal City fuel depot]].<ref name="DUME">{{Rebels|DUME}}</ref>

[[File:TIE_striker_XWM.png|thumb|left|250px|A TIE/sk x1]]
Other experimental TIE models included the [[TIE/ag "Aggressor" Starfighter]], a medium attack craft with a rear-mounted turret, the [[TIE/ph "Phantom" Multi-Role Stealth Starfighter]], a stealth fighter with [[Cloaking device|cloaking]] abilities that saw extremely limited use,<ref name="Starships and Speeders">''[[Starships and Speeders]]''</ref> the [[TIE/sk x1 experimental air superiority fighter]], a fighter designed for optimal atmospheric flight and base defense,<ref name="RO UVG" /> and the [[TIE crawler]], a tank that resembled a TIE cockpit with tank treads replacing its wings.<ref name="CYD2" /> The TIE podracer was designed by the criminal empire of the [[Hutt]] [[Grakkus Jahibakti Tingi]] as a gift for Admiral Rellen.<ref name="Beyond Victory" />

====Mining Guild====
[[File:Mining_Guild_TIE_fighter_SWCT.png|thumb|right|250px|The Mining Guild was allowed to use modified TIE fighters due to its association with the Galactic Empire.]]
The [[Mining Guild]]'s affiliation with the Empire granted it access to certain Imperial resources, including TIE models, which the Guild modified into the [[TIE/mg Mining Guild starfighter]].<ref name="DB MG Fighter">{{Databank|mining-guild-tie-fighter|Mining Guild TIE fighter}}</ref>

====Imperial remnants====
Imperial remnants still utilized TIE fighters following the destruction of the Empire. [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]'s [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]] made use of several [[Outland TIE fighter]]s, which resembled a TIE/ln, but featured wings that folded outwards upon landing.<ref name="Chapter 7">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 7: The Reckoning}}</ref> [[Commodore]] [[Visler Aqorian Korda III]]'s [[Visler Korda's faction|Imperial remnant]] also produced the [[auto-fighter]], a [[drone]] TIE fighter, during its time on [[Rekkana]].<ref name="Hare-Brained Heist">{{IDWAdventuresCite-2017|annual=2019|story=Hare-Brained Heist}}</ref>

===First Order===
The [[First Order Navy]] continued to use TIE fighters based on the Empire's designs. Manufactured by [[Sienar-Jaemus Fleet Systems]], the new TIE models boasted significant upgrades from Imperial technology. The successor to the TIE/ln was the [[TIE/fo space superiority fighter]], which, unlike most TIE models of the Empire, was equipped with basic shielding to protect the [[First Order TIE fighter pilot|pilot]].<ref name="Cross" />

[[File:VonregAndTIEs-StationThetaBlack.png|thumb|250px|left|TIE/fo fighters escort Major Vonreg's TIE Baron into battle.]]
The [[First Order Special Forces]] used the [[TIE/sf space superiority fighter]], another advanced model equipped with a hyperdrive and shields as well as a gunner-operated turret on the underside of the cockpit. The fighter's hull featured red markings to identify its affiliation with Special Forces.<ref name="Cross" /> Also in use were the First Order's [[TIE/se Bomber]]s,<ref name="Allegiance 1">[[Allegiance 1|''Allegiance'' 1]]</ref> a transport called the [[TIE/es assault shuttle]],<ref name="Galaxy's Edge 1">[[Galaxy's Edge 1|''Galaxy's Edge'' 1]]</ref> and a stealth fighter known as the [[TIE/wi Interceptor]].<ref name="TROS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

More elite pilots such as [[Major]] [[Elrik Vonreg]] used the [[TIE/ba Baron Space Superiority Interceptor]], an all-red TIE Interceptor.<ref name="Recruit">{{Resistance|The Recruit}}</ref> Inspired by the TIE Defender, First Order technicians sought to revive heavy weapons capabilities and developed the [[TIE/vn space superiority fighter]], which was tested by only the most elite pilots, including [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]].<ref name="TLJ:ICS">''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> Ren later utilized a [[TIE/wi modified interceptor]] during his time as [[Supreme Leader]].<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars New" />

===Sith Eternal===
The [[Sith Eternal]]'s [[fleet]], the [[Final Order]], used the [[TIE/dg starfighter]], which was identifiable by its triangular wings.<ref name="TROS VD" />

==Behind the scenes==
The TIE line first appeared in the first ''[[Star Wars]]'' film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] of the [[Original trilogy]], in [[1977]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Within ''Star Wars'' [[canon]], it was first identified in the [[2015]] reference book ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' gave the alternate title of "TIE-series,"<ref name="RO UVG" /> but the [[2019]] novel ''[[Thrawn: Treason]]'' would later write this name as "TIE series."<ref name="Thrawn: Treason">''[[Thrawn: Treason]]''</ref>
